pr_title: Get StreamID while still in the MsQuic callback
pr_body:
Incoming connections: Call `GetParam` from `MsQuicStream` ctor (which is called from `MsQuicConnection.NativeCallback`)
Outgoing connections: Get id from `STREAM_START_COMPLETE` event

Fixes #69070.

issue_context.title: [QUIC] Don't use GetParam to get stream ID
issue_context.body:
The operation is expensive on both client (5.0% incl time in HttpClient benchmark) and server (3.7% incl time) -- it seems msquic is waiting on the lock inside

- for client, it should be possible to get stream ID from stream start event
- for server, I believe the data is not available ATM, but I think it might be possible to extend a stream accept event (PEER_STREAM_STARTED.StreamId = PEER_STREAM_STARTED.Stream->Id) -- thoughts @nibanks?

Yes, you might want to cache this locally at your first availability. You can query it anytime after the stream has been started. The stream is considered already started once indicated in the peer_stream_started event. Either get it from a callback, or query it immediately in the callback for the best performance. Querying anything on your own thread always leads to it being queued to the QUIC worker.

if StartCompletionSource.Task throws, we would not null out the stream; we need to check whether that's OK @rzikm 
Could you please check how it behaves in other places (set-unset links to stream or to connection in the state objects); maybe it's better to null it out in places where we complete the TCS?

Why do we need this? It makes me nervous as we had issues with mutual references before.
If it is just to store the `StreamId` then we perhaps should move it to the `State`.
I see, I will create a follow up PR next week.

One more note that the `GetTraceId()` is trying to mimic msquic so it is easier to correlate logs. If StreamId is available, we can make it part of TraceId in addition to what we have. That would make it easier IMHO to correlate with packet captures and Kestrel.
We could make it static and pass the handle to GetStreamId(). But this is fine for now.
I assume that in both directions (incoming/outgoing), the user cannot get a QuicStream instance before `_streamId` is set, correct?
